en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Yasir who said,

‘When Al-Mamoun went out from Khurasan intending Baghdad, and Al-Fazal, the one with two governorships, went out, and we went out with Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, Al-Fazl, the one with the two governorships received a letter from his brother Al-Hassan Bin Sahl, and we were in one of the lodgings, ‘I looked at the changes of the year in the calculations of the stars, and I found therein that you, in such and such a month on the day of Wednesday, would taste the heat of the iron and heat of the fire, and I view that you and Amir Al-Momineen and Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> should enter the bathhouse and perform cupping therein, and splash the blood upon your hands in order to decline its inauspiciousness from you’.

So the one with the two governorships wrote to Al-Mamoun with that and asked him that he should ask Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (to do) that. So Al-Mamoun wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> (to do) that. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wouldn’t be entering the bathhouse tomorrow, nor do I<sup>asws</sup> view for you nor for Al-Fazl that you both should be entering the bathhouse tomorrow’, So he reiterated upon the plan, twice.

Al-Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘O commander of the faithful! I wouldn’t be entering the bathhouse tomorrow, for I<sup>asws</sup> saw Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in this night in the sleep, and he<sup>saww</sup> said to me: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! Do not enter the bathhouse tomorrow’, nor do I<sup>asws</sup> view for you nor for Al-Fazl that you should both enter the bathhouse tomorrow’. So Al-Mamoun wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> speak the truth, O my Chief, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> spoke the truth. I won’t be entering the bathhouse tomorrow, and I shall let Al-Fazl know’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Yasir said, ‘So when we were in the evening and the sun set, Al-Rezaasws said to us: ‘Say, ‘We seek Refuge with Allahazwj from the evil of what would be descending during this night’’. So we did not cease to be saying that. So when Al-Reza prayed the morning Salat, heasws said to me: ‘Ascend upon the roof and listen intently, can you hear anything?’

So when I had ascended, I heard the commotion, and the struggling, and it was increasing. So there we were with Al-Mamoun who had entered from the door which was to his house from the door of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and he was saying, ‘O my Chief! O Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>! May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Recompense you<sup>asws</sup>! With regards to Al-Fazl, so he had refused and had entered the bathhouse, and a group of people came over upon him with the swords, so they killed him; and three of the ones who had come upon him were seized. It was so that one of them was a son of his maternal uncle Al-Fazl Ibn Zul Qalamayn’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So the army, and the leaders, and the ones who were from the men of Al-Fazl gathered at the door of Al-Mamoun and they said, ‘He assassinated him and killed him!’, meaning Al-Mamoun, ‘We are seeking his blood’, and they came with the fire in order to burn the door. So Al-Mamoun said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O my Chief! Can you<sup>asws</sup> come out to them and disperse them?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Yasir said, ‘So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> rode and said to me: ‘Ride’. So I rode. So when we went out from the door of the house, he<sup>asws</sup> looked at the people and they had crowded, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to them by his<sup>asws</sup> hand (gestures): ‘Disperse!’. So they dispersed’. Yasir said, ‘So the people turned back. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Some of them were falling upon the others, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not gesture to anyone except he ran and passed by’.
